title.narrative: Technical assistance to Gorongosa National Park (GNP) on disaster resilient reconstruction and social programs in Gorongosa buffer zone

description.narrative:
In 2019, after Mozambique has been strongly hit by Cyclones Idai and Kenneth, Mozambique Country Office have developed the so-called Building Back Better and Resilience Building Umbrella Programme (2019-2024) with the overall objective to enhance the climate adaptation capacity of Mozambican people and institutions and achieve more resilient human settlements. The Umbrella Programme aims at working as a common and coherent framework that will guide UN-Habitat short, medium and long-term projects, programmes and engagements regarding the post-cyclone reconstruction. It is being operationalized through two complementary axes of interventions to support the recovery and reconstruction process in Mozambique: Axis 1- Building Back Better Safer (BBB) Schools, Hospitals and Resilient Housing and Axis 2 - Enhancing Urban Resilience through Integrated Approaches. UN_Habitat have signed a MoU with the Ministry of Health, and Idai Post Cyclone Reconstruction Cabinet (GREPOC). Also UN-Habitat has signed two AOc with the Ministry od Education. One of the objectives of these agreements is to ensure the implementation of a resilient recovery and reconstruction process of housing and public infrastructure through the provision of continuous Technical Assistance in planning, defining, coordinating, training and supervising the reconstruction process. This project is specifically part of Axis 1 and continues the consolidation of the Safer Schools and Safer Hospitals initiative started in 2012. The project aims to Build Climate Resilience of communities affected by Idai through the support of the Gorongosa National Park (GNP), communities living in the buffer zone and local government structures by supporting the institutional coordination of MINEDH, MISAU and GREPOC and providing technical support during the reconstruction phase to increase the resilience of the school and health network based on the development of disaster adapted infrastructure, improving capacities, knowledge appropriation and the adoption of official technical resilience measures. The Gorongosa National Park and its buffer zone is a large area ( + 6000 km ²) that include districts of Nhamatanda, Dondo, Gorongosa, Muanza, Cheringoma and Maringué in Sofala province. GNP elaborated a programme in collaboration with UN-Habitat to increase resilience of the school and health network based on the development of disaster adapted infrastructure, improving capacities, knowledge appropriation and adoption of resilient technical measures which has been granted with 12 M from USAID. The primary objective of GNP program is to construct resilient infrastructure strong enough to withstand the most common natural hazards. Such buildings will help ensure that communities in the Buffer Zone have structures that can be used as safe havens during emergency situations, particularly when serious flooding and forceful winds are present. Resistant schools and health clinics, which are the focus of this intervention, will also reduce the possibility of disruption to these services during the rainy season. PNB engages UN-Habitat as high-level technical assistance to make use of our experience and expertise in terms of disaster risk reduction strategies, resilient infrastructure, Building Back Better and integrated approach to increase community capacities. In addition, coordination with inter-institutional actors at province and central level is required.
The project approach proposes to intervene in the buffer zone of Gorongosa working at first on a general overview of the spatial/territorial links with the education and health infrastructure network in collaboration with the local communities, government, and the park. Secondly, a vulnerability assessment of the infrastructure will be realized in the target districts aiming to select the schools and health centres to be constructed or rehabilitated .Once pre-selected the infrastructures, the development of technical projects that comply with resilience standards will initiate as base for tender processes. Field activities will start after the first phase of assessment and desk work through participatory approaches, implementation of prioritized durable solutions and disaster preparedness activities such as delineation of evacuation routes, identification of safe places to shelter , early warning system at school level, first aid, simulation exercises and other activities with active participation of students, teachers, nurses and doctors.
UN-Habitat will work together with local communities and government entities to increase their capacities and knowledge on climate change and DRR through their participation during the reconstruction process.
